note: The two statuses that must never be confused, and the two ways a 200 can go. X puts the rotating query id in the request path, so a rotated id names an endpoint that is not there and the origin answers 404; a guest token that does not authorize an operation is answered 403 or 401 instead. Reading either as the other is the failure this table exists to catch.

design rule, wider than the measured row: every operation on this route carries a rotating id in its path, so every one of them can go stale the same way
the 2026-08-10 probes: a guest-blocked operation returns 403 or 401, which is the distinction that makes the 404 above a stale id
